names.confirmation_basis: Company 6-K exhibit filed on EDGAR (6-K dated 2026-08-06) states Rezolve AI 'will report its H1 2026 results and host an investor call on September 1, 2026'. This is the company's own filed document, not an aggregator.
names.priority_reasoning: This is a SEMI-ANNUAL report, not a quarter, from a de-SPAC FPI with zero recoverable earnings-reaction history on EDGAR and a 12% implied move on a 40%-of-mid-wide chain. Revenue is claimed to have gone from $6.32m to ~$127m in twelve months, and essentially nothing about the composition of that number is in the market's hands. Maximum distance between what is priced and what is findable.
names.where_edge_might_live: The balance sheet and the counterparties behind the revenue ramp, not the revenue line. Specifically: (1) trade receivables and DSO in the H1 statements versus the ~$127m pre-announced revenue — a 20x revenue jump with no matching cash collection is the single most checkable thing here; (2) the identity and concentration of the customers driving it (search UK Companies House filings for Rezolve AI PLC and its subsidiaries, and the 6-K/20-F related-party notes); (3) the financing trail — every 6-K and F-1/F-3 since the de-SPAC, share count, warrants, convertible notes and ATM usage, because share count on this name moves; (4) whether the FY2026 $360m guide implies an H2 that is arithmetically implausible against H1 actuals.
names.notes: Semi-annual filer: there is no 10-Q and no 'Q2'. This is the six months ended 2026-06-30 reported on Form 6-K. Baseline has n=0 prior reactions, so the 12.04% implied move has no historical anchor at all. ALREADY IN THE WIRE and not worth re-finding: the ~$127m H1 preliminary revenue and the reaffirmed ~$360m FY2026 guide were both disclosed 2026-08-06; the +16.8% 5-day run-up is likely that. Prior-year comparatives: H1 2025 revenue $6.32m, audited FY2025 revenue $46.8m.

sweep_notes: Nine of ten rows carry a company-sourced date — a very different result from the 2026-08-31 prior run, and the reason is that eight of these nine companies pre-announce by press release and did so between 2026-07-20 and 2026-08-27. Three baseline 'suspect' verdicts were overturned by company sources: CANG (IR page, 2026-08-25), HMR (GlobeNewswire, 2026-08-26) and PXS (GlobeNewswire, 2026-08-26). In all three the 'suspect' flag came from the 6-K text matcher treating monthly operational updates as earnings and inferring a false short cadence; the same artefact makes NIO's 'fits_cadence' verdict and its eight-event reaction history describe monthly delivery reports rather than earnings, which is a defect a hunter must not inherit. RGS is the single unresolved row: it is a real and genuinely due fiscal-Q4/FY2026 print, but Regis has filed no 8-K since 2026-05-13, lists no upcoming event, and released the equivalent FY2025 report on 2025-09-03 — so 2026-09-01 is a vendor projection and should be verified before any budget is spent. Two session corrections that change which trading session carries the reaction: YEXT is company-confirmed BMO despite seven of its eight prior prints being AMC, and HMR is confirmed BMO despite all six priors being AMC. One session I could not settle: CANG's release time on 2026-08-31 — the IR page gives the date but not the hour, and its Q1 call was intraday at 12:30 p.m. ET, so the amc label is not established. Structural notes worth carrying forward: RZLV is a SEMI-ANNUAL foreign private issuer, so 2026-09-01 is an H1 report on Form 6-K and there is no 'quarter'; MMED's print is its second ever and lands beside both a Medtronic split-off window and an IPO lock-up expiry falling on or about 2026-09-02; CANG's 10-for-1 share consolidation of 2026-07-21 invalidates its unadjusted per-share history. Five of ten names (CANG, HMR, RGS, and effectively YEXT and ZEPP whose chains are 93% and 109% of mid) have no usable statement of what the market priced, so their baseline 'expected_move' figures are historical medians and not implied moves. Tooling: WebFetch worked for sec.gov, ir.cangoonline.com, investors.yext.com and regiscorp.com; heidmar.com/investors returned 404 (the announcements archive path works instead); WebSearch returned three transient 'unavailable' errors and was retried with different phrasing. No figure in this file is unsourced; where a claim rests on a search snippet rather than a fetched document the underlying company or SEC URL is listed in confirmation_urls.
